scale_012:n1.prompt:
You are helping me draft candidate company-level OKRs for the upcoming quarter, to be tracked in Linear or Notion. Before starting, ask me for: (1) our company name and current quarter/year, (2) access to or summaries of last quarter's OKR results and any performance/metrics docs (e.g., revenue, growth, product usage, retention data), (3) any strategic priorities or board/leadership notes I want factored in, and (4) which tool (Linear or Notion) we use so drafts match its OKR structure.

Using this input, please:
1. Summarize last quarter's objective outcomes (met/missed/partial) and pull out 3-5 notable trends or gaps.
2. Draft 3-5 candidate company-level Objectives for the new quarter, each with 2-4 measurable Key Results. Objectives should be qualitative and inspirational; Key Results should be specific, numeric, and time-bound.
3. For each candidate objective, note the rationale (what data or prior result it responds to) and any tension or tradeoff with other drafted objectives.
4. Format the draft in a way that's ready to paste into Linear or Notion (title, description, key results as sub-items).
5. Compile a short checklist for leadership review: open questions, assumptions made, and any missing data that limited the draft.

Do not finalize, publish, or commit these OKRs anywhere, and do not mark any as approved — company objectives require leadership's explicit judgment and sign-off. Once the draft and checklist are ready, present them to me and stop for human sign-off. Report back with: the summarized prior-quarter analysis, the full draft objectives and key results, the rationale notes, and the review checklist, clearly labeled as a draft pending leadership approval.

scale_012:n2.prompt:
You are helping me set up a quarterly OKR tracking system in {{vendor}}, our project-management tool. Please prepare everything needed but stop for human sign-off before any changes are applied, since approval is required before changes go live.

First, ask me for: (1) my {{vendor}} workspace/site details if not already accessible with your configured credentials, (2) the current quarter and company objectives (or ask me to supply a draft list if none exist), and (3) the team names that should have their own OKR sections.

Then prepare a plan for a new OKR database/workspace structure in {{vendor}} that includes:
- A top-level 'Objectives' view organized by level (Company, Team, Individual)
- For each objective: fields for owner, owning team, status, priority, and linked key results
- Key Results as sub-items or linked records with fields for target metric, current progress, and status
- A dashboard or summary view showing overall progress by team and by quarter
- A shared docs/notes section alongside the tracker for context, meeting notes, or check-in summaries

Draft the exact database schema (property names and types), the page/view hierarchy, and sample entries populated with the company objectives I provide, so everything is ready to create with one approval. Do not create or modify anything in {{vendor}} yet.

When your draft is ready, report back with: the proposed database structure, sample populated entries, and the dashboard/view layout, clearly labeled as a proposal awaiting my review. Explicitly state that you are pausing and will stop for human sign-off before applying any changes in {{vendor}}.

scale_012:n3.prompt:
You are helping me prepare Team OKRs for the current quarter, drafted for team-lead review inside our existing Notion or Linear workspace (use whichever tool we already track OKRs in). If you don't have them, ask me for: (1) the company-level OKRs document link or content, (2) the specific team name, (3) the team lead's name/handle, (4) the workspace/tool we use (Notion page or Linear project), and (5) any known team capacity constraints or in-flight priorities for the quarter.

Once you have these, using your configured credentials to access the workspace: review the company objectives and key results, then draft 2-4 team objectives with 2-4 measurable key results each that plausibly ladder up to the company OKRs while respecting the team's stated capacity and priorities. Write these as a clearly labeled draft (e.g., 'DRAFT - Pending Team Lead Approval') in the appropriate Notion page or Linear project, matching the existing structure/format used for other teams' OKRs. Include a short rationale note under each objective explaining how it connects to a company OKR.

Do not mark these OKRs as final, do not notify the broader team, and do not change their status from draft. The team lead must review, adjust, and explicitly commit to the specific goals and metrics since they own the resourcing tradeoffs — this remains a human step. Prepare everything needed for a fast review (draft objectives, key results, rationale, and a summary comparison to company OKRs), then stop for human sign-off.

Report back with: a link to the drafted OKRs, a summary of each objective and its key results, and any open questions or capacity risks you flagged for the team lead to resolve before approval.

scale_012:n4.prompt:
You are helping me set up quarterly OKR tracking in {{vendor}}. Our company OKRs have already been drafted with objectives and their associated key results. If you don't have this list yet, ask me for it now (I'll provide each objective and its key results, along with the owning team for each, if not already documented in {{vendor}} or shared notes).

Goal: For each key result, prepare a corresponding project in {{vendor}} using your configured credentials, so key results can be tracked with status, priority, an owning team, and individual tasks.

For each key result, please:
1. Draft a project named after the key result text (or a concise version of it).
2. Set a description linking it to its parent objective for context.
3. Assign the owning team if known; otherwise flag it for me to specify.
4. Set an initial status (e.g., "Not Started" or your workspace's equivalent) and a priority level matching the KR's importance.
5. Set up or confirm workflow statuses/custom fields that match how our team tracks progress, if not already configured.
6. Draft a few starter tasks under each project where the key result implies obvious first actions, leaving assignee and due date fields blank or with placeholder suggestions for me to confirm.

Compile a summary list showing: KR name → proposed project name, owning team, status, priority, and any starter tasks drafted, plus any KRs where information (team, priority) is missing and needs my input.

Do not create or apply any of these projects, statuses, or tasks in {{vendor}} yet — only prepare drafts and the summary. Since a human must explicitly approve before changes are applied, stop for human sign-off once your draft summary is ready, and wait for my review and approval before creating anything.

scale_012:n5.prompt:
You are helping me send the kickoff announcement for our new quarterly OKR framework to the team via {{vendor}}. Company, team, and individual objectives will be tracked in Linear/Notion, and this message announces that rollout.

Before drafting, ask me for anything missing: (1) the target channel name or ID in {{vendor}}, (2) the OKR cycle/quarter this applies to, (3) the top 2-3 company-level objectives to highlight, (4) where OKRs will live (Linear/Notion link if available), and (5) any key dates (e.g., when team/individual OKRs are due).

Then draft a clear, concise kickoff message that: states we're adopting a quarterly OKR framework, names the current quarter, lists the company objectives I gave you, explains that teams and individuals will set aligned OKRs tracked in Linear/Notion, includes the tracking link if provided, and states the deadline for team/individual OKRs to be entered.

Prepare the message to be sent using {{vendor}}'s messaging capability (either the official API with a scoped token or an incoming webhook, using your configured credentials) targeting the channel I specify. Do not actually post the message yet — present the final drafted text, the exact channel it will go to, and the method (API vs webhook) you'll use, and stop for human sign-off before sending.

Once I approve, send the message and report back confirming it was posted successfully, including the channel name, timestamp, and a copy of the final text sent. If posting fails, report the error and do not retry without my direction.
